page: Microsoft Azure M32ts is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 38 MB of L3 cache, 192.0 GB of memory (6.0 GB per vCPU), and 1100 GB of local SSD storage. It operates without a GPU and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, provisioned through Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a clear distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded computational capabilities. Single-core tests reflect lower-tier performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 914.0 and stress-ng single-core reaching 1038.78. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads utilize the 32 dedicated execution threads effectively, delivering average-tier results such as 8438.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 21904.52 in stress-ng multi-core, and 100.31 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The processor supports AVX-512F and AES instructions, achieving 10031.24 in PassMark CPU encryption tests.

The memory subsystem yields 106.41 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and 45.13 GB/sec in write bandwidth, backing consistent data throughput. Operational metrics show 20.68 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark database score of 8947.75, and 17.69 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Natural language inference on smaller models maintains 944.78 prompt tokens per second, though throughput scales down significantly to 3.6 tokens per second on 70B parameter models.

The primary tradeoff of the M32ts is modest per-core throughput balanced against substantial memory density and bundled local storage. This profile provides solid qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense, multi-threaded applications rather than single-thread-limited processes. Workloads best matched to this configuration include in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, relational database systems, and multi-threaded data engineering jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure M32ts is a memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs from a 16-core Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of RAM and 1100 GB of local SSD storage. Engineered without an accelerator GPU, the instance leverages Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates lower-tier single-core throughput alongside mid-tier multi-threaded scalability, scoring 8438.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 21904.52 in stress-ng multi-core. The memory architecture delivers 106.41 GB/sec of uncached read bandwidth, supporting operational throughput of 20.68 million Redis SET operations per second and 17.69 GB/sec for static web serving. While limited on single-thread execution speeds, the system provides high memory capacity relative to compute allocations. The M32ts is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, relational database hosting, Redis key-value caching layers, and multi-threaded batch data transformations.
